title: TD3B: Transition-Directed Discrete Diffusion for Allosteric Binder Generation
claim: Ligands with opposite functional effects bind the same kind of target but drive it into different conformational states.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right, ligand and labeled arrow between before/after structures
description: Two stacked rows, labeled (A) and (B), each showing a before-and-after binding transition from left to right. In (A), a blue ribbon-style receptor protein appears at left. A small red helical peptide ligand sits above a black arrow labeled 'Agonist binding'. At right, the same blue protein has the red ligand docked in its pocket, labeled 'Active State'. In (B), a teal protein appears at left. A small yellow ball-and-stick ligand sits above an arrow labeled 'Antagonist binding'. At right, the teal protein has the yellow ligand bound, labeled 'Inactive State'. The color coding separates the two cases: blue and red for agonist, teal and yellow for antagonist. The eye goes first to the large protein structures and the bold labels.
caption: Structural mechanisms of agonist and antagonist peptide binding. (A) Agonist binding (red) triggers conformational shifts in the target protein (blue) to its Active State, initiating downstream signaling. (B) Antagonist binding (yellow) stabilizes the Inactive State by occupying the binding pocket without inducing structural changes, effectively blocking signal activation.
abstract: Protein function is often controlled by ligands that bias the direction of state transitions, such as agonists and antagonists, rather than stabilizing a single conformation. This is especially important for clinically relevant G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), where therapeutic efficacy depends on functional directionality. Structure-based design methods optimize binding to static conformations and cannot represent non-reversible, directional effects or systematically distinguish agonist from antagonist behavior. To address this gap, we introduce Transition-Directed Discrete Diffusion for Allosteric Binder Design (TD3B), a sequence-based generative framework that designs binders with specified agonist or antagonist behavior via a directional transition control objective. TD3B combines a target-aware Direction Oracle, a soft binding-affinity gate, and amortized fine-tuning of a pre-trained discrete diffusion model, enabling targeted agonist and antagonist generation decoupled from binding affinity and unattainable by equilibrium-based or inference-only guidance baselines. The code and checkpoints are available at https://huggingface.co/ChatterjeeLab/TD3B.
